title: The Script, Word for Word
summary: Every line of the Medicare script, every branch, why each question is asked, and how to deliver it.

lessons.title: The Opening & Parts A and B

blocks.html: You read the script exactly as written. Not close. Exact. The opening does three jobs: it greets the consumer, says who you are and that the call is recorded, and asks the first qualifying question: do they have Medicare Parts A and B?

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: Hey, good morning/afternoon (Customer Name)?

lines.speaker: consumer
lines.text: Yeah, who's this?

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: Hey (Customer Name), this is _______, I'm with America's Health on a recorded line. We were just giving you a quick call today about your food and utility card that you never received. That card, it IS exclusively for members who have Medicare Parts A and B. You DO still have your Medicare Parts A and B, correct?

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: (Let them confirm)

lines.speaker: consumer
lines.text: Yes, I do.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: Yes - (continue) to the double-confirm.

lines.speaker: consumer
lines.text: No, I don't have Medicare.

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: There must have been a mistake. Thank you for your time, have a great day.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: (Code as DQ)

lines.speaker: consumer
lines.text: Parts A and B? I don't know what that means.

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: I understand. Well, do you have the red, white and blue card by chance?

lines.speaker: consumer
lines.text: Oh, the flag card? Yeah, I have that.

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: Okay, perfect, so then you DO have Medicare Parts A and B, correct?

lines.speaker: consumer
lines.text: I guess so, yes.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: (If yes, skip to 'Do you receive Medicaid') - you already confirmed the card, so you don't double-confirm it again.

blocks.title: Recorded line, every time
blocks.html: The opening says you're with America's Health on a recorded line. That is a compliance requirement. Never skip it or rush past it.

blocks.question: A consumer says "I don't know" when you ask about Parts A and B. What do you say next?
choices: There must have been a mistake. Thank you for your time, have a great day.
I understand. Well, do you have the red, white and blue card by chance?
Perfect, and do you receive Medicaid along with your Medicare plan?
Okay, LAST question here, do you have insurance through your work or the VA?
blocks.explanation: For "I don't know," ask about the red, white and blue card. If yes, confirm Parts A and B and skip to the Medicaid question.

blocks.question: After an "I don't know" consumer confirms the card and then confirms Parts A and B, where do you go?
choices: Read the double-confirm card line
Read the DNC disclaimer
Skip to the Medicaid question
Ask for the transfer
blocks.explanation: The script says: if yes, skip to 'Do you receive Medicaid'.

blocks.html:
Next you double-confirm that they have the red, white and blue card. Why? People confuse Medicare with other insurance. The card question helps make sure they really have Medicare, and it is a compliance step: double confirm Medicare Parts A and B.

If they have a different card, ask whether they have their Medicare number. If they don't, or they lost the card, ask whether they know their Medicare number or Social Security number. Either way, you continue with the script.

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: Okay, perfect, and JUST to double confirm, that IS the red, white and blue card, correct?

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: (Let them confirm)

lines.speaker: consumer
lines.text: Yep, that's the one.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: Yes - (continue) to Medicaid.

blocks.title: Branch: I have a different card

lines.speaker: consumer
lines.text: No, I've got a Humana card.

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: Okay, no problem, but you DO have your Medicare number, correct?

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: (If yes, continue. If no, read the No line below.)

blocks.title: Branch: No / I'm not giving my number out / I lost it

lines.speaker: consumer
lines.text: I lost that card years ago.

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: Okay, you WOULD have to know your Medicare number or Social Security number to review those increases. You don't need to give it to me, but the licensed agent may need it. Do you know either of those?

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: (Either way, continue)

blocks.title: You are NOT collecting their number
blocks.html:
You NEVER ask the consumer to read or give you their Medicare number or Social Security number. The script only asks whether they know one of them. The licensed agent handles the actual numbers.

Never ask them to read it to you, and never write it down. "You don't need to give it to me" is part of the line for a reason.

blocks.question: A consumer says "I have a different card, it's from my plan." What do you say?
choices: I understand. Well, do you have the red, white and blue card by chance?
Okay, no problem, but you DO have your Medicare number, correct?
There must have been a mistake. Thank you for your time, have a great day.
Okay, perfect, and JUST to double confirm, that IS the red, white and blue card, correct?
blocks.explanation: For a different card, ask if they have their Medicare number. If yes, continue; if no, read the No line ("you WOULD have to know...").

blocks.question: You read the "you WOULD have to know your Medicare number or Social Security number" line and the consumer doesn't know either one. What do you do?
choices: Code as Not Interested
Code as DQ
Continue with the script to the Medicaid question
Read the DNC disclaimer
blocks.explanation: The script says: either way, continue. You never ask them to read or give you the number.

lessons.title: Medicaid, State & ZIP, Work or VA

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: Perfect, and do you receive Medicaid along with your Medicare plan?

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: Yes/No - (continue)

blocks.html: Why ask about Medicaid? People with both Medicare and Medicaid may have different plan options. Either answer continues. It is never a DQ by itself.

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: Perfect, thanks so much for confirming that for me. So yeah, it DOES look like you may be ENTITLED to some additional food benefits since the food prices have gone up. If that's sent, I DO still have you out in (state), with the zip code (zip code), correct?

lines.speaker: consumer
lines.text: Yes, still in Ohio.

blocks.html: Why confirm state and ZIP? Plans and benefits vary by area, so the specialist needs the right location. Confirming it is also a compliance step. Notice the line says you may be ENTITLED. That word matters.

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: Okay, LAST question here, do you have insurance through your work or the VA?

lines.speaker: consumer
lines.text: No, just Medicare.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: No - (continue) to the transfer ask.

lines.speaker: consumer
lines.text: Yes, I still have my insurance from my job.

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: Oh, there must have been a mistake. Thank you for your time, have a great day.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: (CODE AS DQ)

blocks.question: What is the LAST qualifying question before you ask for the transfer?
choices: Okay, LAST question here, do you have insurance through your work or the VA?
I DO still have you out in (state), with the zip code (zip code), correct?
Perfect, and do you receive Medicaid along with your Medicare plan?
Okay, perfect, and JUST to double confirm, that IS the red, white and blue card, correct?
blocks.explanation: The script literally says "LAST question here" for work or VA insurance.

blocks.question: A consumer says yes, they have insurance through the VA. What do you say?
choices: I understand, but MANY people are finding out RIGHT now that they ACTUALLY qualify for WAY more than they're receiving.
No problem, I'll add you to our internal do not call list immediately and you won't receive any further calls from our company. We do apologize for any inconvenience, have a great day.
Oh, there must have been a mistake. Thank you for your time, have a great day.
Perfect, well that is EVERYTHING I need.
blocks.explanation: Work or VA yes: read "Oh, there must have been a mistake..." and code as DQ.

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: Perfect, well that is EVERYTHING I need. So, a Medicare specialist is coming on the line now to review the additional food benefits for you. Give them JUST a few minutes to go over them with you, okay?

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: AFFIRM - STOP and wait for a verbal yes. Do NOT click transfer until they say yes.

lines.speaker: consumer
lines.text: Okay, sure.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: Yes - NOW click transfer and continue to the ringing line.

lines.speaker: consumer
lines.text: No, I don't want to be transferred.

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: No - do NOT click transfer. Read an EXTRA NOT INTERESTED rebuttal, then go back to the ask.

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: Well, I understand, but you've worked your whole life for these Medicare benefits. Give the agent JUST a few minutes to review and compare your plan to make SURE you're not missing out on ANYTHING you may be entitled to.

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: Give them JUST a few minutes to go over them with you, okay?

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: Wait for the yes. Only click transfer once they say yes.

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: Alright, so you'll hear a little bit of ringing, that's just me connecting them in, and once they pick up they'll ask you for your name, okay?

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: (You already have their permission to transfer. You do NOT need to ask for another okay here or once the licensed agent connects.)

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: In the meantime, how's that weather out there today?

lines.speaker: note
lines.text: (FLUFF AWAY) - keep light small talk going while it rings. When the specialist picks up, stop talking.

blocks.title: No yes, no transfer
blocks.html:
"Give them JUST a few minutes to go over them with you, okay?" is the ONLY time you ask for permission on the call. The consumer MUST say yes before you click transfer.

  • Yes: click transfer and read the ringing line.
  • No: don't transfer. Read an EXTRA NOT INTERESTED rebuttal, then go back to the ask and wait for the yes.

That yes is your permission. The "okay?" at the end of the ringing line is not a second permission ask, and you don't need another confirmation once the licensed agent connects.
"Fluff away" means make friendly small talk (like the weather) while the line rings. It keeps the consumer relaxed and on the line so they don't hang up during the ringing.

blocks.question: The consumer says "No" when you ask them to give the specialist a few minutes. What do you do?
choices: Start the whole script over from the opening
Don't transfer. Read an EXTRA NOT INTERESTED rebuttal, then go back to "Give them JUST a few minutes to go over them with you, okay?"
Transfer them anyway
Code the call as DQ
blocks.explanation: No: read an EXTRA NOT INTERESTED rebuttal and go back to the ask. Never click transfer without a yes.

blocks.question: When do you click the transfer button?
choices: As soon as you finish reading the transfer ask
Only after the consumer says yes to "Give them JUST a few minutes to go over them with you, okay?"
After the ringing line, whether or not they agreed
Right after they confirm their ZIP code
blocks.explanation: The consumer MUST say yes to the transfer ask before you click transfer. No yes, no transfer. That yes is enough: there is no second confirmation after the licensed agent connects.

blocks.html:
Knowing the words is half the job. How you say them is the other half.

  • Energy. Smile when you talk. People can hear it. Flat, tired voices get hang-ups.
  • Emphasis. The CAPITALIZED words in the script (IS, DO, JUST, EVERYTHING, LAST) are there on purpose. Punch them. They make the line sound confident and certain.
  • No pauses. Keep moving. Long pauses give the consumer time to doubt, get distracted, or hang up.
Practice this line out loud. Hit the capitalized words:

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: Okay, perfect, and JUST to double confirm, that IS the red, white and blue card, correct?

lines.speaker: agent
lines.text: Okay, LAST question here, do you have insurance through your work or the VA?

blocks.title: Flow from question to question
blocks.html: When the consumer answers, say "Perfect" and roll straight into the next line. Most lines already start with "Perfect" or "Okay" to help you do that.

blocks.question: Why are some words in the script in CAPITAL letters?
choices: They are typos you should fix
They are words to say quietly
They are words you can skip
They are words to emphasize when you speak
blocks.explanation: Capitalized words are emphasis cues. The script stays exactly as written.

blocks.question: Why should you avoid pausing between script lines?
choices: Pauses give the consumer time to doubt, get distracted or hang up
The dialer disconnects after a pause
Pauses are only allowed on Fridays
Pauses are a compliance violation by themselves

questions.question: What is the very first line of the script?
choices: Good morning, do you have a minute?
Hey, good morning/afternoon (Customer Name)?
Hi, is this the homeowner?
Hello, this is Medicare calling.
questions.explanation: The script starts: "Hey, good morning/afternoon (Customer Name)?"

questions.question: Which company does the script say you are with?
choices: The state Medicaid office
Medicare
Social Security
America's Health
questions.explanation: You are with America's Health on a recorded line. Never claim to be Medicare or the government.

questions.question: What is the correct order of the qualifying questions?
choices: Card, work or VA, Medicaid, Parts A and B, state and ZIP
Medicaid, Parts A and B, work or VA, state and ZIP, card
Parts A and B, red white and blue card, Medicaid, state and ZIP, work or VA
State and ZIP, Parts A and B, card, work or VA, Medicaid
questions.explanation: Parts A and B, double-confirm the card, Medicaid, state and ZIP, then the LAST question: work or VA.

questions.question: A consumer says No, they don't have Medicare Parts A and B. What do you say?
choices: Perfect, and do you receive Medicaid along with your Medicare plan?
I understand. Well, do you have the red, white and blue card by chance?
I understand, but MANY people are finding out RIGHT now that they ACTUALLY qualify for WAY more than they're receiving.
There must have been a mistake. Thank you for your time, have a great day.
questions.explanation: No to Parts A and B: read the mistake line and code as DQ.

questions.question: What comes right after the Medicaid question?
choices: Asking about work or VA insurance
Asking for the transfer
Double-confirming the card
Confirming their state and ZIP code
questions.explanation: After Medicaid comes the state and ZIP line.

questions.question: Which line is the exact transfer ask?
choices: Perfect, so I'm going to transfer you now to Medicare to get your benefits, okay?
Perfect, well that is EVERYTHING I need. So, a Medicare specialist is coming on the line now to give you your food card. Stay on the line, okay?
Perfect, well that is EVERYTHING I need. So, a specialist is going to call you back later, okay?

Perfect, well that is EVERYTHING I need. So, a Medicare specialist is coming on the line now to review the additional food benefits for you. Give them JUST a few minutes to go over them with you, okay?
questions.explanation: The transfer ask must be read verbatim, including telling them a Medicare specialist is coming on the line.

questions.question: What do you say while the line is ringing?
choices: Nothing; stay completely silent while it rings.
Please hold while I introduce you.
Please don't hang up or you'll lose your benefits.
In the meantime, how's that weather out there today?
questions.explanation: Fluff away with "In the meantime, how's that weather out there today?" Then go silent once the specialist picks up.

questions.question: A consumer says "I lost my card." What do you say?
choices: There must have been a mistake. Thank you for your time, have a great day.
Okay, perfect, so then you DO have Medicare Parts A and B, correct?

Okay, you WOULD have to know your Medicare number or Social Security number to review those increases. You don't need to give it to me, but the licensed agent may need it. Do you know either of those?
Oh, there must have been a mistake. Thank you for your time, have a great day.
questions.explanation: No / I'm not giving my number out / I lost it: read the "you WOULD have to know" line, then continue either way.

questions.question: A consumer answers "Yes" to the Medicaid question. What happens?
choices: Read the DNC disclaimer
Continue to state and ZIP
Skip straight to the transfer
Code as DQ
questions.explanation: Yes or No to Medicaid both continue.

questions.question: What does "FLUFF AWAY" mean?
choices: Put the consumer on mute
Make light small talk while the transfer rings
Skip the rest of the script
Explain the benefits in detail
questions.explanation: Fluff means friendly small talk (like the weather) to keep the consumer relaxed while it rings.

questions.question: How should you treat CAPITALIZED words like IS, DO and JUST?
choices: Whisper them
Skip them
Replace them with your own words
Emphasize them
questions.explanation: Capitals are emphasis cues. Punch them with energy.

questions.question: An "I don't know" consumer confirms the card and Parts A and B. What do you read next?
choices: Okay, perfect, and JUST to double confirm, that IS the red, white and blue card, correct?

Perfect, well that is EVERYTHING I need. So, a Medicare specialist is coming on the line now to review the additional food benefits for you. Give them JUST a few minutes to go over them with you, okay?
Okay, LAST question here, do you have insurance through your work or the VA?
Perfect, and do you receive Medicaid along with your Medicare plan?
questions.explanation: The script says skip to 'Do you receive Medicaid'.
